steps.content:
07:18, July 22, N.F. 113
Flowerdale High Street, near Erica Villa, Eastside
Since the attack, the shopping street has been eerily quiet in the morning. Most of the sheriffs are guarding Shalom's villa, leaving only a few unlucky stragglers to patrol the surrounding areas.

On the other side of the rainy street, a woman holding flowers is walking alone down the quiet pavement. She nods to the familiar sheriffs as she passes by them, not bothering to inquire about their worries.
She walks all the way to the tailor shop. Upon finding the door unlocked, she freezes for a moment, then closes her umbrella and walks inside with a smile.

steps.speaker: Female Tailor
steps.content: It's too early for business. I wasn't expecting anyone. You scared me a bit.

steps.speaker: Female Tailor
steps.content: Hello, dear customer. This shop is closed right now. If you want a custom made dress, please come back in a few days.
Rahu doesn't respond. She watches as the shop owner puts her flowers in a vase—they're white carnations.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Those flowers are very beautiful.

steps.speaker: Female Tailor
steps.content: ...Thank you. My husband loved carnations. He was fond of the color purple, and said it reminded him of me.

steps.speaker: Female Tailor
steps.content: He worked for the FAC. He retired for several years due to his injuries, but then got called to help out with the emergency in Syndicate. And that... led to his funeral.
The woman chokes up, turning her head to wipe her tears.

steps.speaker: Female Tailor
steps.content: Sorry. I just came back from the cemetery, so I'm still feeling quite emotional.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: I understand.

steps.speaker: Female Tailor
steps.content: Really? Did something similar happen to you, miss?

steps.speaker: Female Tailor
steps.content: Judging from your uniform, you're part of the FAC too, right...? Though I can't make you a dress right now, you're welcome to take any flowers you like.

steps.speaker: Female Tailor
steps.content: If there are people you'd like to mourn, too...

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: ...There are.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: But it's not time to mourn them yet.
Rahu goes to the window and draws the curtains.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Maybe you don't know, but the situation in West District is really bad. Many have died, and it's taking quite a while to deal with the contaminated corpses. Memorial services have been postponed for some time already. If your husband died there, he won't be buried until next month.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Where exactly did you go mourn him, ma'am?
Before she finishes her sentence, a shield comes flying forth, smashing the floorboards under her feet. White carnation petals scatter everywhere, yet the tailor is no longer standing where she was.
A few streaks of silver light zip towards Rahu, who blocks them with her shield. She looks over at the attacker—the mourning widow now has a sinister yet teasing look on her face.

steps.speaker: Female Tailor?
steps.content: Sigh, how impatient you are. I could've explained a small discrepancy like that.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: No need. Your dodging skills have already explained everything.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: We've fought several times, Miss <color=#fb9259>Assassin</color>. Your silhouette is quite memorable.

steps.speaker: Female Tailor?
steps.content: Hehe, quite the sense of humor, eh? You're in good spirits, Miss Bodyguard. Take off your mask and let me see... are you smiling?

steps.speaker: Female Tailor?
steps.content: Then I hope you keep smiling for the rest of your life...

steps.speaker: Female Tailor?
steps.content: Sometimes, a lifetime passes in the blink of an eye.
The woman twirls the needle in her hand and jabs it into the back of a mannequin, activating a hidden trigger with a click. The mechanism starts to attack Rahu!
